title: Daily Market Briefing
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Defensives bid, semis dumped.
Money hid in staples and healthcare while SOXX -5.63% and DRAM -7.28% got liquidated; the Nasdaq's 0.80% drop with QQQ put-call at 1.43 says this was hedging, not broad panic. Hike odds at 60.4% into tomorrow's FOMC kept duration and gold offered.

INDICES — VIX 17.1, above its 15.5 20-day MA.
RSP +0.07%, DIA -0.25%, IWM -0.34%, SPY -0.45%, QQQ -0.80%, SOXX -5.63%. Small > large by 0.11pp. Crude +1.14% and gold -1.49% were the loudest cross-asset prints. SPY sits below its 200-day MA — a CTA sell trigger.

VOLUME & BREADTH — SOXX 1.6x, IWM 1.4x, IJH 1.3x led gainers; GLD 0.6x and SLV 0.8x went quiet.
SPY printed 1.1x and QQQ 1.1x — flat tape. SOXX volume up with price down -5.63% is outright distribution. Breadth diverges badly: only 38% of the S&P is above its 50-DMA, up/down volume 0.84, and 49 new 60-day lows against 11 highs — narrow, deteriorating internals beneath a flat index.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLC Comms +2.19%, XLV Healthcare +1.45%, XLP Staples +1.25%, XLI Industrials +0.00%, XLF Financials +0.00%, XLE Energy +0.00%, XLY Discretionary -0.10%, XLRE Real Estate -0.69%, XLB Materials -0.90%, XLU Utilities -1.34%, XLK Technology -1.81%.
CIBR +5.99% and IGV +5.04% topped industries; DRAM -7.28% and SOXX -5.63% bottomed. Flows contradict price: XLU +$711mm (98th pct) and XLB +$632mm (100th) drew the heaviest 5-day inflows while XLF bled -$1,587mm (2nd pct) and XLP -$726mm — buyers chased the two worst performers. Money is rotating defensively but flows lag price, and software (IGV +5.04%) is quietly catching up while semis break — AI hardware fading / high-to-low rotation.

POSITIONING — QQQ put-call 1.43 screams protection demand; SPY's 0.84 and IWM's 0.56 show complacency elsewhere. SPY skew +12.6% and QQQ +15.6% price real downside fear into tomorrow. VIXEQ 36.0 sits below its 36.8 20-day MA against VIX above its own — implied correlation is compressed, a rotation tape, not a macro one.

CROSS-ASSET — WTI +1.14% and the dollar +0.36% together crushed gold -1.49% and silver -2.20% — a real-rates squeeze, not a haven bid. Next FOMC is Sep 16. CME FedWatch prices hold 39.6%, cut 0.0%, hike 60.4%; Polymarket shows 93% for a 2026 hike, +16pp in five days.

SIGNALS & WATCH — Fear & Greed 48.7, neutral.
TER -13.30% on "unfavorable news," GEV -8.62% after GLJ Research's Sell, PANW +13.09%, BAC -5.14%. VRT -7.65% on 2.3x volume is distribution; AON +2.92% on 2.2x is accumulation. Watch FDN +1.31% on 2.3x volume, TER's 2.1x volume wipeout, and QQQ's 1.43 PCR into the FOMC.
